 By Max Saltman , Kevin Liptak , Julia Vargas Jones , Jennifer Hansler

 The United States will issue visas to the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, and his family, allowing “them entry into the United States,” a State Department official told CNN.
 Two sources earlier confirmed to CNN that Bolsonaro had left Brazil and headed to the US after losing Sunday’s presidential election. A US official initially told CNN that Bolsonaro was headed to Florida, but later said his exact destination in the US was unclear.
 A Brazilian source close to Bolsonaro said that the politician had feared arrest in Brazil. He is currently under investigation by the country’s highest court for alleged acts of corruption, money laundering and currency evasion.
 Brazil’s Federal Police canceled Bolsonaro’s passports after he failed to surrender them, affiliate CNN Brasil reported.
 Speculation about his movements mounted after Argentine news outlet Infobae reported that Bolsonaro had left Brazil via Argentina after losing Sunday’s runoff presidential election against leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The Argentine government said in a statement that it has “no record of Flávio Bolsonaro entering” the country.
 Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered Bolsonaro to turn in his passports within 24 hours on Monday. CNN has reached out to Bolsonaro, his political party and the Brazilian Federal Police for comment on the senator’s whereabouts.
 Related article
 Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva speaks after winning the presidential runoff in Sao Paulo, Brazil, on October 25, 2026. 
 Amanda Perobelli/Reuters 
 How Lula beat Bolsonaro, broke records and halted the region’s right-wing wave 
 8 min read 
 Bolsonaro said Brazilian police had informed him of the order in person and told him he was banned from leaving Brazil. In a video posted to Instagram, the senator denied that he intended to flee.
 One of the allegations against Bolsonaro is connected to potential illegal online betting platforms, and another to the production of a biopic about his father, “Dark Horse,” which federal police believe involved funds from Banco Master, a now-collapsed bank at the heart of a $7 billion Ponzi-like scheme in 2025. Bolsonaro denies all wrongdoing.
 At the time of his departure from Brazil, there were no warrants for his arrest, but according to legal analysts, the act of defying the court’s orders to surrender his passports could be enough reason for a warrant to be issued.
 Right-wingers in exile
 In leaving Brazil for the US, Bolsonaro joins a large community of Brazilian conservatives in exile – including his own brother Eduardo, former Brazilian intelligence chief Alexandre Ramagem and podcaster Paulo Figueiredo.
 Eduardo suggested shortly before the runoff election that Flávio ought to leave Brazil if his bid for the presidency failed. On Tuesday, Eduardo called rumors that his brother had fled a “lie.”
 Flávio’s journey mirrors his father’s actions after losing the 2022 presidential election. Shortly after his loss, Jair Bolsonaro decamped for Orlando, Florida , where he remained for three months. During that time, hundreds of his supporters stormed the seats of power in the capital Brasília, vandalizing the supreme court, congress and the presidential palace in an attack reminiscent of the insurrection on the US Capitol in 2021.
 Bolsonaro and his allies’ efforts to overturn the 2022 election results led to the former president being sentenced to 27 years in prison . US President Donald Trump, a prominent supporter of the Bolsonaro family, briefly imposed tariffs on Brazil in response to the criminal case against Jair. Trump claimed without evidence earlier this week that Lula’s victory was “rigged.”
 Bolsonaro’s leaving Brazil comes directly after his surprise loss to Lula over the weekend . The conservative politician was a strong favorite to win, but Lula managed to outmaneuver Bolsonaro Sunday, earning 4.4 million more votes in the second round. Bolsonaro initially refused to concede to Lula, saying his team would ask for the results to be annulled.
 Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party reversed course days later. “We recognize the presidential election results,” party head Valdemar Costa Neto said, according to CNN Brasil. “But we believe the issues ⁠raised need to be properly clarified.”
 CNN’s Mauricio Torres and Anabella Gonzalez contributed reporting.
